mutants.intent: safe_evaluate returns ALLOW instead of DENY when evaluate() raises an unexpected exception.
mutants.property: an unexpected gate fault must fail closed as DENY (kill_active); the fault wrapper may never produce an ALLOW decision.

mutants.intent: the kill switch only adds KILL_ACTIVE when the envelope is already invalid, so a valid envelope ignores kill.
mutants.property: an active kill switch (explicit or ACL_SUPPLY_GATE_KILL) must DENY every evaluation, whatever the envelope contains.

mutants.intent: when the envelope carries a ref, the observed HEAD is no longer compared to the pinned digest (trust the ref).
mutants.property: the post-checkout HEAD must exactly equal expected_sha; a mutable ref is never a substitute for the pin and a mismatch is DENY (head_mismatch).

mutants.intent: the presence of untrusted prose counts as a performed verify, so no observed HEAD plus prose drops verify_missing and records verify_performed=true.
mutants.property: verify_performed and verify_missing derive only from an observed full-digest HEAD; marketplace or agent prose is data and cannot stand in for verification.

mutants.intent: an empty allowed-origins set skips the origin check, turning an empty allowlist into allow-all.
mutants.property: an origin not in the allowlist is DENY (origin_not_allowlisted); an empty allowlist admits no origin and there is no implicit allow-all.

mutants.intent: PinnedSource.pinned accepts any non-empty pin string, so a short or malformed pin counts as pinned.
mutants.property: an MCP server or hook pin must be a full 40/64-hex digest; a short or malformed pin is unpinned and DENY (mcp_server_unpinned / hook_update_unverified).

mutants.intent: a remote (never-pinnable) MCP server triggers MCP_SERVER_UNPINNED only when every declared server is remote, so one remote server is masked by pinned local ones.
mutants.property: a single remote MCP server (http / sse / streamable-http) in the manifest is DENY (mcp_server_unpinned) regardless of how the other servers are pinned and observed.

mutants.intent: drop the glob-character check on a permission head, so Ba*, B?sh and *ash are no longer treated as a shell grant.
mutants.property: a permission head containing a glob character may expand to a shell-class tool on the host and must be DENY (skill_shell_preapproved).

mutants.intent: an entry without a full-digest pin is skipped during observed-digest matching instead of failing it, so an unpinned hook (or MCP server) is accepted.
mutants.property: every declared hook and MCP server must carry a full-digest pin equal to the adapter-observed digest; an unpinned entry is DENY (hook_update_unverified / mcp_server_unpinned).

mutants.intent: NFKC normalisation of permission strings is disabled, so a compatibility-form spelling of a shell word is no longer folded to ASCII before shell matching.
mutants.property: a fullwidth or compatibility spelling of a shell word (e.g. U+FF22 U+FF41 U+FF53 U+FF48) must be classified as a shell grant (skill_shell_preapproved), not merely as an unparseable rule.

mutants.intent: a weak or unknown update mode is silently normalised to pin_and_verify with weak_attempt=False instead of being reported.
mutants.property: a weak update mode (trust_ref, auto_latest, skip_verify, ...) must be returned as a weak attempt and DENY (update_policy_rejected); it is never honoured as pin_and_verify.

mutants.intent: evaluate_update_policy ignores weak_attempt, so a pin_and_verify policy carrying a waive flag (auto_update, skip_verify_on_update) passes.
mutants.property: a waive flag in the update policy is DENY (update_policy_rejected) even when the mode itself is pin_and_verify.
